The second Problem paragraph (p.3) presents the workaround of giving maintainers full administrative rights, which reviewers read as a solution or alternative.

The same mechanism is called 'drift check' in Section 4.2 (p.7) and 'drift report' in the Schedule (p.9).
The same servers are called 'compute hosts' (Abstract, Problem) and 'Linux hosts' (Introduction, Figure 3).
The text uses both 'administrative rights' (Introduction, Problem) and 'administrative privileges' (Abstract, Figure 1 caption) for the same concept.
The Problem section (p.3) calls maintainers 'supervisors', while the rest of the proposal uses 'maintainers'.
The system is called 'self-service platform' (Abstract) and 'access management platform' (Figure 1 caption).
The spelling of 'e-mail' is reported as inconsistent (Abstract p.2, Schedule p.9).
First-person singular 'I' is used throughout the Abstract, Objective, Schedule, and Transparency sections (unlocated across the document).

The abbreviation 'API' in Section 4.1 (p.6) is reported as used without prior definition.
